title: Training at Scale: Memory, Precision and Parallelism
summary: A 7B model needs about 16 bytes of GPU memory per parameter to train with Adam, before counting activations, so even modest models do not fit on one GPU. This lesson does the memory arithmetic, explains mixed precision and activation checkpointing, shows how data, tensor and pipeline parallelism and ZeRO split the work, and ends with the learning-rate schedule that keeps it all stable.
objectives: Break training memory into weights, gradients, optimizer states and activations, and compute the 16 bytes per parameter of mixed-precision Adam
Explain FP32, FP16 and BF16 and why master weights stay in FP32
Estimate activation memory per layer and the saving and cost of gradient checkpointing
Compute per-GPU memory under ZeRO stages 1 to 3 and the pipeline bubble for a given number of micro-batches
Write the warmup-plus-cosine learning-rate schedule and evaluate it at any step
prerequisites: You should know how parameters are counted ([The Transformer Block](/learn/model-foundations/transformer-block)), what gradient descent and backpropagation do ([How a Network Learns](/learn/model-foundations/how-networks-learn)), and how much compute a run needs ([Scaling Laws and Compute Budgets](/learn/training-and-adaptation/scaling-laws)).
